definition: Rapport means an easy mutual understanding between people.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word rapport. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know rapport should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By the third session the physical therapist had an easy rapport with the wary linebacker, who now saved his best jokes for her.
Civility stops short of rapport — courteous, correct, and completely surface, the ease strangers manage in an elevator, while a rapport is earned, mutual, and particular to its pair.
Intimacy goes further than rapport — a rapport reads a colleague's pauses; intimacy holds the private history behind them.

Chemistry is the instant, unexplained spark between two people — present at the first exchange or not at all, and nobody can say quite why. Rapport is the buildable version: an ease two people earn session by session until each trusts what they read in the other.

An understanding is the plain knowledge of how someone works — what they need, when to push, when to wait — and it accumulates only through time spent together. Rapport is that knowledge grown warm: mutual, trusting, and specific to the pair who earned it.

The documentary crew wanted one interview above all: Elias Brandt, the last dory fisherman on the island, who had turned away every reporter for thirty years.
The director sent no camera at first.
She sent Ana, a junior producer, who simply showed up at the dock each morning and learned to coil line.
For six weeks Ana asked nothing.
She handed tools, hauled crates, and let the old man correct her knots.
By July he was correcting her jokes instead.
The rapport between them was built, not found — a trust earned in small mornings, until each could read the other's silences.
When the camera finally came, Brandt spoke for four hours.
The film's best moments are answers to questions she never had to ask aloud.
